questions.question: A student examines a plant cell under a microscope and identifies small, green structures within the cytoplasm. What are these structures, and in which part of the plant are they most abundant?
options: Mitochondria, found mostly in the root cells
Chloroplasts, found mostly in the leaf cells
Vacuoles, found mostly in the stem cells
Ribosomes, found mostly in the flower cells

questions.question: If a chemical inhibitor specifically blocks all metabolic activity within the chloroplasts of a plant cell, which of the following cellular processes will directly stop first?
options: Active transport of mineral ions
Cellular respiration using glucose
Synthesis of proteins on ribosomes
The process of photosynthesis

questions.question: Some mutant plants have pale yellow leaves because they lack the pigment chlorophyll inside their chloroplasts. What primary difficulty will these plants experience?
options: They will be unable to absorb water from the soil.
They will be unable to absorb light energy needed for photosynthesis.
They will be unable to release carbon dioxide into the air.
They will be unable to transport sugar to their roots.

questions.question: How does the thinness of a typical deciduous plant leaf directly facilitate the process of photosynthesis?
options: It allows light to penetrate all the way through to the cells containing chloroplasts.
It prevents water from evaporating too quickly from the upper surface.
It provides mechanical flexibility to prevent the leaf from snapping in the wind.
It maximizes the storage space for excess starch within the leaf.

questions.question: Lily pads float flat on the surface of a pond and have very broad, wide leaves. What is the main evolutionary advantage of this large surface area?
options: To maximize the absorption of light for photosynthesis
To increase the rate of water absorption from the pond
To allow the plant to float more easily on the water surface
To prevent herbivorous fish from eating the leaf tissue

questions.question: A scientist seals a healthy green plant in a glass jar under bright light. After several hours, the concentration of carbon dioxide inside the jar decreases significantly. What is the reason for this change?
options: The plant is releasing carbon dioxide as a waste product of photosynthesis.
The plant is taking in carbon dioxide from the air to use in photosynthesis.
Carbon dioxide is condensing into liquid water on the leaves.
The plant is converting carbon dioxide into mineral salts in the soil.

questions.question: During an experiment, bubbles of gas are seen escaping from the leaves of an underwater Elodea plant exposed to light. What gas is being released, and what is its source?
options: Carbon dioxide, produced as a waste product of respiration
Oxygen, produced during photosynthesis and released into the surroundings
Nitrogen, absorbed by the roots and excreted through the leaves
Water vapor, produced by transpiration from the leaf surface

questions.question: In plants, carbon dioxide enters the leaf while oxygen and water vapor exit. What is the scientific term used to describe this dual process of gases moving in and out of the leaf?
options: Osmosis
Translocation
Gas exchange
Respiration

questions.question: If a researcher applies a thick, impermeable layer of petroleum jelly to the underside of a leaf where most of the small holes called stomata are located, what will be the immediate effect on the plant?
options: Gas exchange will be severely restricted, reducing photosynthesis.
The leaf will absorb more light energy because of the shiny surface.
The roots will stop taking up water due to increased pressure.
The plant will produce more glucose to compensate for the sealed holes.

questions.question: By what physical mechanism do carbon dioxide molecules move from an area of higher concentration in the atmosphere into the lower concentration inside an open stoma of a leaf?
options: Active transport requiring cellular energy
Diffusion, where molecules move randomly down a concentration gradient
Osmosis through a semi-permeable membrane
Capillary action driven by water surface tension

questions.question: In a terrestrial food web, oak trees are classified as producers. What biological characteristic defines them as producers?
options: They consume decomposing organic matter from the soil.
They make their own food using the process of photosynthesis.
They rely on insects to provide them with essential sugars.
They absorb organic food molecules directly through their bark.

questions.question: A farmer moves potted tomato plants into a completely dark shed for several days. What will happen to the process of photosynthesis during this time?
options: It will continue at the same rate using heat energy from the shed.
It will switch to using soil nutrients instead of atmospheric gases.
It will stop completely because photosynthesis can only happen in the presence of light.
It will speed up because the plants do not have to contend with UV radiation.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes the nature of photosynthesis inside a plant cell?
options: It is a single, instantaneous physical change that occurs on the leaf surface.
It is a series of chemical reactions that take place inside specific plant cells.
It is a passive physical filtration process that cleans the air.
It is a purely mechanical process of water transport driven by evaporation.

questions.question: If you were to group the substances involved in photosynthesis into starting materials (reactants) and resulting substances (products), which group is correct?
options: Reactants: oxygen and glucose; Products: water and carbon dioxide
Reactants: water and glucose; Products: carbon dioxide and oxygen
Reactants: water and carbon dioxide; Products: oxygen and glucose
Reactants: carbon dioxide and oxygen; Products: water and glucose

questions.question: We often write 'carbon dioxide + water -> glucose + oxygen' to describe photosynthesis. Why is this word equation considered a scientific 'model'?
options: It is a simplified word summary representing a complex series of many chemical reactions.
It is an exact, physical replica of a chloroplast that can be viewed under a microscope.
It is a hypothetical guess that has not yet been proven by experiments.
It lists only the toxic waste products that the plant must get rid of.

questions.question: A student grows four identical plants under different conditions. Plant A gets light, air, water, and minerals. Plant B gets no light. Plant C gets no water. Plant D gets no air. Which plant is most likely to survive and grow healthy over a long period?
options: Plant B, because darkness stimulates root growth.
Plant C, because plants can make their own water from gases.
Plant A, because plants need light, air, water, and minerals to stay alive.
Plant D, because plants only need soil minerals to grow.

questions.question: How do the different parts of a plant cooperate to obtain the necessary resources for survival?
options: Roots take in light and water, while leaves take in minerals and gases.
Leaves take in light and gases from the air, while roots take in water and minerals from the soil.
Leaves take in minerals and water, while roots absorb light from the darkness of the soil.
Both leaves and roots can absorb light, air, water, and minerals equally.

questions.question: Why can we not classify the water and dissolved minerals absorbed by a plant's roots as 'food' for the plant?
options: Because water and minerals are not organic nutrients that provide energy, yet plants still need food to survive and grow.
Because plants only use water and minerals to anchor themselves in the soil.
Because water and minerals are toxic to plants in large quantities.
Because plants convert water and minerals directly into carbon dioxide.

questions.question: Unlike animals, which must eat other organisms, how do green plants obtain their food?
options: They absorb pre-made sugar molecules directly from the surrounding soil.
They are producers that make their own food rather than taking it in from their surroundings.
They capture and ingest microscopic insects through microscopic pores in their roots.
They absorb organic humus from decaying leaf litter through their leaves.

questions.question: Once a plant has successfully performed photosynthesis, what is the nature and purpose of the food it has produced?
options: It is a mineral salt used to increase water absorption in the roots.
It is a carbohydrate, which the plant uses for growth and as a source of energy.
It is a gaseous oxygen molecule used to repel herbivorous pests.
It is a protein used exclusively to form the outer waxy cuticle of the leaf.

questions.question: If you look at a cross-section of a green leaf under a light microscope, which cellular structures would you expect to find inside many of the leaf cells?
options: Vacuoles containing chlorophyll
Chloroplasts containing genetic material
Chloroplasts as distinct intracellular structures
Stomata floating inside the cytoplasm

questions.question: A scientist isolates different compartments of a plant cell to find where the chemical conversion of light energy into chemical energy occurs. In which structure does this synthesis happen?
options: In the cell wall
In the chloroplasts
In the vacuole
In the cytoplasm outside any organelles

questions.question: Why are chloroplasts able to capture light energy for the process of photosynthesis?
options: They contain chlorophyll, which absorbs light
They are transparent, which reflects light
They contain starch, which traps light
They have cell walls that refract light

questions.question: How does the thinness of a typical deciduous plant leaf benefit the cells located in its middle layers?
options: It reduces the amount of water lost by evaporation from the upper surface
It allows sufficient light to penetrate through to cells containing chloroplasts
It makes it easier for roots to transport minerals directly to the surface
It prevents carbon dioxide from escaping out of the leaf too quickly

questions.question: What is the primary evolutionary advantage of a plant having leaves with a broad, flat surface area rather than thick, needle-like structures in a shaded forest?
options: To increase the rate of water absorption from rain
To maximize the absorption of light for photosynthesis
To allow more minerals to enter the leaf directly from the air
To store greater amounts of carbohydrate within the leaf structure

questions.question: During a sunny day, which gas must a plant take in from the surrounding atmosphere through its leaves to carry out photosynthesis?
options: Oxygen
Water vapour
Nitrogen
Carbon dioxide

questions.question: During photosynthesis, what happens to the oxygen gas that is produced as a result of the chemical reactions inside the leaf cells?
options: It is completely converted into glucose inside the chloroplasts
It is released from the leaves as a gas into the air
It is transported to the roots to absorb minerals
It is stored permanently in the vacuole of the cell

questions.question: What term is used to describe the biological process where carbon dioxide gas enters a plant leaf and oxygen gas is released?
options: Transpiration
Gas exchange
Respiration
Osmosis

questions.question: Through which microscopic structures on the leaf's surface does the primary exchange of carbon dioxide and oxygen gases occur?
options: Chloroplasts
Root hairs
Stomata
Veins

questions.question: By what physical mechanism do carbon dioxide and oxygen molecules travel through open stomata into and out of the leaf?
options: Active transport powered by cell energy
Osmosis across a selectively permeable membrane
Diffusion down a concentration gradient
Bulk flow driven by root pressure

questions.question: Why are green plants classified as ecological producers?
options: They absorb pre-made organic food from the soil using their roots
They make their own food using a process called photosynthesis
They break down dead matter to release nutrients into the environment
They consume other organisms to obtain carbohydrates

questions.question: If a healthy green plant is kept in a completely dark room with plenty of water and carbon dioxide, what will happen to its rate of photosynthesis?
options: It will continue at a lower rate using stored heat energy
It will stop completely because photosynthesis can only happen when there is light
It will increase to compensate for the lack of light
It will remain constant because only temperature affects the reaction

questions.question: Which statement best describes the nature of photosynthesis as it occurs inside plant cells?
options: It is a single, instantaneous physical change of state
It is a series of chemical reactions that take place inside cells
It is a purely physical process of filtering gases from the air
It is a mechanical breakdown of nutrients absorbed by the roots

questions.question: If you were to list the chemical inputs (reactants) and outputs (products) of photosynthesis, which of the following is correct?
options: Reactants: oxygen and glucose; Products: water and carbon dioxide
Reactants: water and carbon dioxide; Products: oxygen and glucose
Reactants: light and minerals; Products: carbon dioxide and water
Reactants: water and glucose; Products: oxygen and carbon dioxide

questions.question: The word equation 'water + carbon dioxide -> glucose + oxygen' is widely used in science. What does this word summary represent?
options: A literal, single-step reaction that bypasses cell structures
A model of the process of photosynthesis, which actually involves many chemical reactions
An exact physical description of how gases dissolve in water
A recipe for plants to absorb nutrients directly from the soil

questions.question: To stay alive, grow, and remain healthy, which combination of resources must a green plant obtain from its environment?
options: Light, air, water, and minerals
Soil, glucose, oxygen, and shade
Fertiliser, warmth, starch, and carbon dioxide
Light, sugar, oxygen, and clay

questions.question: How do plants divide the task of acquiring resources from their environment between their roots and their leaves?
options: They take in water and light through leaves, and gases and minerals through roots
They take in light and gases through leaves, and water and minerals through roots
They take in minerals and light through leaves, and gases and water through roots
They take in all resources through their roots and none through their leaves

questions.question: A student claims that plants do not need food because they take in water and mineral ions from the soil. Why is this claim incorrect?
options: Water and minerals are food, but plants also need to eat soil particles
Water and minerals are not food, but plants do need food to stay alive and grow
Water and minerals are the only food plants need, but they must be digested first
Plants do not need food at all; they only require energy from minerals

questions.question: How do plants obtain the food they require for survival and growth compared to animals?
options: They absorb organic glucose directly from rich soil through root hairs
They do not take in food from their surroundings; they are producers that make their own food
They ingest microscopic insects and fungi present on their leaves
They absorb dissolved carbohydrates from water in the soil

questions.question: What type of substance is the food made by plants during photosynthesis, and what do they primarily use it for?
options: It is mineral salts, used to construct cell walls and absorb water
It is carbohydrate, which they use for growth and as a source of energy
It is protein, which they use to absorb light from the sun
It is carbon dioxide gas, which they store in their roots for respiration

questions.question: If you were to examine a thin slice of a typical green leaf under a microscope, which of the following best describes the organization of the leaf's cells?
options: The entire leaf is a single large cell containing many nuclei and chlorophyll molecules floating freely.
The leaf is composed of numerous individual cells, many of which contain distinct internal structures called chloroplasts.
The leaf contains cytoplasm and cell walls, but chloroplasts only form in the spaces between cells when light is present.
The leaf is made of specialized water-transporting tubes that contain chloroplasts instead of normal plant cell components.

questions.question: A scientist treats a plant cell with a chemical that specifically disables only the chloroplasts while leaving all other organelles fully functional. What is the most direct consequence of this treatment on the cell's processes?
options: The cell will lose its ability to carry out photosynthesis.
The cell will no longer be able to absorb minerals through active transport.
The cell will instantly stop absorbing water by osmosis.
The cell will be unable to transport sugar to other parts of the plant.

questions.question: Why does a mutant plant that lacks chlorophyll in its chloroplasts appear white and fail to grow, even when kept in a warm, well-watered room with plenty of sunlight?
options: Without chlorophyll, the plant cannot absorb carbon dioxide through its roots.
Without chlorophyll, the chloroplasts cannot absorb the light energy needed to drive photosynthesis.
Without chlorophyll, water molecules cannot enter the leaves through the stomata.
Without chlorophyll, the chloroplasts cannot release stored glucose into the soil.

questions.question: Which of the following explains why most leaves are very thin rather than thick and blocky?
options: To allow water vapor to condense on the upper surface of the leaf more quickly.
To prevent carbon dioxide from escaping out of the bottom of the leaf.
To ensure light can penetrate through the layers of cells to reach the chloroplasts inside.
To reduce the amount of surface area exposed to wind damage.

questions.question: Some plants grow in very shady forest floors. How does having broad, flat leaves with a large surface area benefit these plants in their native habitat?
options: It helps the leaves catch falling rain more effectively before it reaches the roots.
It reduces the rate of gas exchange to prevent the leaf from cooling down too much.
It prevents insects from landing on the leaf and eating the photosynthetic tissue.
It maximizes the amount of light the leaf can capture for photosynthesis in low-light conditions.

questions.question: If a plant is kept in a sealed glass jar filled with pure nitrogen and oxygen gas, but completely lacking carbon dioxide, what will happen to its photosynthetic activity?
options: Photosynthesis will stop because the leaves cannot take in carbon dioxide from the air.
Photosynthesis will increase because oxygen is a vital reactant.
Photosynthesis will continue normally because plants produce their own carbon dioxide internally from water.
Photosynthesis will slow down slightly but will be compensated for by absorbing extra minerals.

questions.question: During a sunny day, an aquatic plant is observed producing small bubbles that rise to the water's surface. What is the origin and identity of the gas in these bubbles?
options: It is carbon dioxide being absorbed from the water to fuel respiration.
It is hydrogen gas produced when minerals are broken down by the roots.
It is oxygen gas made during photosynthesis, which is released from the leaves.
It is water vapor being boiled away by the heat of the sunlight.

questions.question: In a plant leaf, carbon dioxide moves inward from the air while oxygen moves outward into the atmosphere. What is the scientific term used to describe this dual process?
options: Transpiration
Mineral absorption
Osmotic balance
Gas exchange

questions.question: If you coat the underside of a leaf with a thick layer of clear wax, the plant's rate of gas exchange drops dramatically. What structure has the wax blocked?
options: Chloroplasts
Root hairs
Stomata
Cell walls

questions.question: How do carbon dioxide and oxygen molecules physically travel through the open stomata of a leaf?
options: They are actively pumped by tiny muscles surrounding each pore.
They move from areas of higher concentration to lower concentration by diffusion.
They travel in water currents pulled up from the roots.
They are pushed through by changes in air pressure caused by the wind.

questions.question: Why are green plants classified as 'producers' in an ecosystem?
options: They produce heat that keeps the surrounding soil warm for decomposers.
They absorb nutrients from dead organic matter in the soil to manufacture glucose.
They make their own food internally using a process called photosynthesis.
They actively hunt and capture microscopic organisms to convert them into sugars.

questions.question: A farmer notices that during a week of thick, dark volcanic ash blockouts, her crops stop growing and their sugar levels drop. Why is photosynthesis unable to take place during this time?
options: The temperature of the air is too high for root absorption.
The plants are forced to switch to absorbing food from the soil.
Without light, plants cannot absorb water through their leaves.
Photosynthesis can only happen when there is light.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the nature of photosynthesis?
options: It is a series of chemical reactions that take place inside plant cells.
It is a single, instantaneous physical change that occurs on the outer surface of the leaf.
It is a physical filtration process that separates pure water from mineral solutions.
It is a mechanical process of breaking down soil particles inside the roots.

questions.question: An isotope-labeling experiment tracks the atoms involved in photosynthesis. Which of the following correctly pairs the starting materials (reactants) with the final substances formed (products)?
options: Reactants: oxygen and glucose; Products: water and carbon dioxide
Reactants: water and carbon dioxide; Products: oxygen and glucose (a carbohydrate)
Reactants: nitrogen and minerals; Products: carbon dioxide and water
Reactants: glucose and carbon dioxide; Products: oxygen and water.

questions.question: Scientists often write 'carbon dioxide + water -> glucose + oxygen' to represent photosynthesis. Since photosynthesis actually involves dozens of complex steps, what is the purpose of this word summary?
options: It is a physical replica of the chloroplast's internal structure.
It is a simplified model of the process that summarizes the overall reactants and products.
It is an exact recipe showing every single individual reaction that takes place in sequence.
It is a mathematical equation used to calculate the speed of light absorption.

questions.question: To investigate what keeps a plant healthy, a student places a potted plant in a sealed, completely dark, airless box with dry soil. Which combination of missing factors will prevent the plant from staying alive and growing?
options: Light, air, water, and minerals
Sugar, warmth, soil particles, and oxygen gas only
Only light and water, since minerals and air are optional for plants
Only nitrogen gas and organic food sources from the surroundings

questions.question: A plant is grown in a setup where its roots are suspended in a sealed, dry chamber filled with carbon dioxide, while its leaves are exposed to water, minerals, and light in an upper chamber. Why will this plant fail to grow properly?
options: Plants must take in light and gases through their roots, and water through their leaves.
Plants take in light and gases from air through their leaves, and take in water and minerals through their roots.
Roots are only capable of absorbing gases like carbon dioxide and cannot absorb liquid water.
Leaves are the only parts of the plant that can absorb minerals from the surroundings.

questions.question: A student argues: 'Since plants absorb water and minerals from the soil, they do not need any food to stay alive.' Why is this statement scientifically incorrect?
options: Water and minerals are actually high-energy carbohydrates that act as food.
Water and minerals are not food, but plants do need food to stay alive and grow.
Plants do not need water and minerals at all; they only require organic food from the soil.
Plants get all of their food by absorbing tiny pieces of organic matter through their roots.

questions.question: If you analyze the soil surrounding a healthy, growing oak tree, you will find no sugars or carbohydrates. How does the tree obtain the food it needs to survive?
options: It takes in food directly from the air through its stomata as pre-made sugar molecules.
It absorbs food from the roots of neighboring plants through fungal networks.
Plants do not take in food from their surroundings, they are producers that make their own food.
It converts minerals in the soil directly into sugar before absorbing them.

questions.question: Once a plant has successfully performed photosynthesis, what is the nature and purpose of the food it has produced?
options: It is a mineral solution used to strengthen the outer bark of the stem.
It is a protein gas released into the air to repel herbivores.
It is water vapor stored in the leaves to keep the plant cool during hot days.
The food that plants make is carbohydrate, which they use for growth and as a source of energy.

questions.question: Under a high-powered light microscope, a student observes a cell from the middle layer of a green leaf. Which of the following describes the correct relationship between the leaf, cells, and chloroplasts?
options: Chloroplasts contain leaves, which are made up of individual green cells.
The leaf is an organ made of cells, and these cells contain many smaller structures called chloroplasts.
Chloroplasts are cells that join together to form the tissue of the leaf.
Cells are made of leaves, which are built from smaller units called chloroplasts.

questions.question: A plant biologist uses a chemical that specifically disables only the chloroplasts in a leaf cell while leaving all other cell parts intact. What is the direct consequence of this on the cell's function?
options: The cell can no longer absorb water through its membrane.
The cell will be unable to carry out the process of photosynthesis.
The cell will stop respiring but will continue to make its own food.
The cell will lose its rigid shape and collapse immediately.

questions.question: Some plants have leaves with white stripes that lack the pigment chlorophyll. How does this affect the function of the chloroplasts in those white regions?
options: They can still photosynthesise because they contain chloroplasts, even without chlorophyll.
They cannot absorb light efficiently, preventing photosynthesis in those areas.
They absorb more light to compensate for the missing pigment.
They absorb oxygen instead of carbon dioxide to perform photosynthesis.

questions.question: Why is the thinness of a typical deciduous plant leaf an important adaptation for its survival?
options: It allows water to evaporate as quickly as possible from the lower surface.
It reduces the weight of the leaf so that the stem does not bend under gravity.
It allows light to penetrate all the way through to the cells containing chloroplasts.
It prevents insects from laying eggs inside the leaf tissue.

questions.question: Two plants of the same species are grown in different light conditions. Plant A has broad, wide leaves, while Plant B has narrow, needle-like leaves. Why does Plant A's leaf structure give it an advantage in a shady environment?
options: Its larger surface area allows it to absorb more of the limited light available.
Its larger surface area prevents water from escaping during the day.
Its wide shape allows it to store more oxygen within its tissues.
Its broad structure makes it easier for wind to shake off harmful pests.

questions.question: A researcher seals a plant in a clear glass jar with normal air. After several hours in the light, the level of carbon dioxide inside the jar decreases significantly. What is the reason for this observation?
options: The plant is releasing carbon dioxide through its roots into the soil.
The plant's leaves are taking in carbon dioxide gas from the air to use in photosynthesis.
Carbon dioxide is condensing into liquid water on the leaves.
The plant is converting carbon dioxide directly into mineral salts.

questions.question: During an experiment, an aquatic plant is placed under water in a beaker under a bright light. Bubbles are seen forming on the leaves and rising to the surface. What is the identity and origin of this gas?
options: Carbon dioxide, which is taken in by the leaves from the water.
Hydrogen, which is produced by the roots and travels up the stem.
Oxygen, which is made during photosynthesis and released as a gas from the leaves.
Water vapour, which is evaporating from the leaf surface.

questions.question: During the day, a plant leaf simultaneously absorbs carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and releases oxygen into it. What is the scientific term used to describe this dual process of swapping gases?
options: Transpiration
Gas exchange
Cellular respiration
Osmosis

questions.question: If a scientist applies a waterproof, non-toxic wax to the underside of a leaf where most of the small holes called stomata are located, what will be the immediate effect on the leaf's processes?
options: It will increase the rate of photosynthesis because water is trapped inside.
It will prevent gas exchange from occurring efficiently because the stomata are blocked.
It will speed up the absorption of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.
It will cause the leaf to absorb more minerals from the surrounding air.

questions.question: How do carbon dioxide and oxygen molecules move into and out of a leaf through open stomata?
options: They are pumped actively by transport proteins in the cell walls.
They are carried by water currents flowing out of the leaf.
They move randomly down concentration gradients by the process of diffusion.
They are pulled in by magnetic forces generated by chlorophyll.

questions.question: Why are green plants classified as 'producers' in an ecosystem?
options: They produce oxygen for themselves to consume as food.
They make their own food using a process called photosynthesis.
They gather food from the soil and produce seeds from it.
They decompose dead organic matter to produce energy.

questions.question: A healthy green plant is kept in a warm, moist room with plenty of carbon dioxide, but in complete darkness for a week. What will happen to its ability to perform photosynthesis?
options: It will perform photosynthesis at a slower rate using heat energy instead.
It will not photosynthesise at all because the process can only happen when there is light.
It will photosynthesise normally because it has plenty of water and carbon dioxide.
It will reverse the process and make carbon dioxide from glucose without needing light.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes the nature of photosynthesis?
options: It is a physical change where water and carbon dioxide dissolve into each other.
It is a single, instantaneous physical reaction that occurs on the leaf surface.
It is a series of chemical reactions that take place inside specific plant cells.
It is a mechanical process of filtering nutrients from the air.

questions.question: A student wants to identify the starting materials (reactants) and the resulting substances (products) of photosynthesis. Which of the following lists them correctly?
options: Reactants: oxygen and glucose; Products: water and carbon dioxide.
Reactants: water and carbon dioxide; Products: oxygen and glucose.
Reactants: light and chlorophyll; Products: water and carbon dioxide.
Reactants: minerals and oxygen; Products: glucose and water.

questions.question: Why do scientists use the word equation 'carbon dioxide + water -> glucose + oxygen' if photosynthesis actually consists of many complex, individual steps?
options: Because the individual steps are not chemical reactions.
The word summary serves as a simplified model of the overall process.
Because glucose and oxygen are not actually produced in the real reactions.
The word equation describes a completely different process that happens in animals.

questions.question: A student grows a plant in a sealed, completely evacuated vacuum chamber (no air) with plenty of water, light, and fertile soil. The plant soon dies. Why did this happen?
options: Plants are living organisms that require air, alongside light, water, and minerals, to survive and grow.
Plants do not need air, but they cannot grow in soil without artificial fertilisers.
The plant died because it did not receive any organic food from the soil.
The vacuum chamber prevented gravity from pulling water into the roots.

questions.question: How do the different parts of a plant cooperate to obtain the resources needed for survival?
options: Roots take in light and gases, while leaves take in water and minerals.
Roots take in water and minerals, while leaves take in light and gases from the air.
Leaves take in water and minerals, while the stem takes in gases and light.
Roots take in gases, while leaves take in minerals and water.

questions.question: A classmate argues that because a plant takes in water and mineral salts from the soil, it does not need any other source of food. Why is this argument incorrect?
options: Water and minerals are toxic to plants if they do not have food to neutralise them.
Water and minerals are not food, but plants still require food to stay alive and grow.
Minerals are a type of food, but water is not, so the plant only feeds on minerals.
Plants get their food directly by absorbing organic matter from dead animals in the soil.

questions.question: Which of the following represents a fundamental difference between how plants and animals obtain their food?
options: Plants absorb ready-made food molecules through their roots, whereas animals ingest food through a mouth.
Plants do not take in food from their surroundings; they are producers that make their own food.
Animals produce their own food internally using heat, whereas plants must eat soil.
Plants convert minerals directly into light energy to feed themselves.

questions.question: What is the nature and purpose of the food substance produced by a plant during photosynthesis?
options: It is a mineral salt used to strengthen the cell walls.
It is a carbohydrate, which the plant uses for growth and as a source of energy.
It is carbon dioxide gas, which is stored in the leaves to prevent wilting.
It is water, which is stored in the roots to keep the plant hydrated.
